pathway.title: HTML
pathway.description: A complete standalone HTML course with practical lessons, examples, guided activities and assessment.

course.title: HTML — Advanced
course.dependencies: A modern browser; no framework required.
course.short_description: A complete standalone HTML course with practical lessons, examples, guided activities and assessment.
course.prerequisites: Comfort with HTML fundamentals and the previous level.
learning_outcomes: Build correct, meaningful and accessible interfaces.
Apply the course concepts in practical projects.
Test, review and explain design decisions.

topics.title: How HTML documents work
topics.description: HTML gives a browser a structured document. Start with doctype, html, head and body, then add meaningful elements inside the body. A document should communicate its purpose through headings, landmarks and content order before visual styling is added.

lesson.title: How HTML documents work
objectives: Explain how html documents work using clear terminology.
Apply how html documents work in a small practical task.
Test and explain the result of the implementation.

blocks.title: Concepts and practical context
blocks.body: HTML gives a browser a structured document. Start with doctype, html, head and body, then add meaningful elements inside the body. A document should communicate its purpose through headings, landmarks and content order before visual styling is added.

blocks.title: A small practical example
blocks.expected_output: A browser page titled Marian with one main heading.
blocks.explanation: Read the example line by line. Identify the structure, the rule being demonstrated, and the part you could change safely.

blocks.title: Guided practical activity
instructions: Create a valid page for a Kenyan school club with a title, one main landmark and a clear heading.
success_checks: The implementation matches the stated goal.
The learner checks both a normal case and one boundary case.
The learner can explain the important lines or declarations.

items.prompt: Which choice best demonstrates the idea in How HTML documents work?

choices.text: Use semantic document structure and a meaningful heading.
Add unrelated code until the page appears different.
Skip testing because the example worked once.

items.explanation: The correct choice applies the concept deliberately and checks its result.

topics.title: Semantic elements and hierarchy
topics.description: Semantic elements describe the role of content. Use headings in a sensible hierarchy and landmarks such as header, nav, main and footer. This helps people, search engines and assistive technology understand the page.

lesson.title: Semantic elements and hierarchy
objectives: Explain semantic elements and hierarchy using clear terminology.
Apply semantic elements and hierarchy in a small practical task.
Test and explain the result of the implementation.

blocks.title: Concepts and practical context
blocks.body: Semantic elements describe the role of content. Use headings in a sensible hierarchy and landmarks such as header, nav, main and footer. This helps people, search engines and assistive technology understand the page.

blocks.title: A small practical example
blocks.expected_output: A page with labelled navigation, main content and a section.
blocks.explanation: Read the example line by line. Identify the structure, the rule being demonstrated, and the part you could change safely.

blocks.title: Guided practical activity
instructions: Turn a plain list of school information into header, navigation, main, section and footer elements.
success_checks: The implementation matches the stated goal.
The learner checks both a normal case and one boundary case.
The learner can explain the important lines or declarations.

items.prompt: Which choice best demonstrates the idea in Semantic elements and hierarchy?

choices.text: Choose elements for meaning rather than appearance.
Add unrelated code until the page appears different.
Skip testing because the example worked once.

items.explanation: The correct choice applies the concept deliberately and checks its result.

topics.title: Links, images and media
topics.description: Links should describe their destination. Images need useful alternative text when they convey information. Decorative images can use empty alt text. Media should have controls and a meaningful context.

topics.title: Accessible forms
topics.description: Forms collect information through labelled controls. A label should identify its input, and related controls can be grouped. Native HTML validation provides useful first-line feedback.

practical_project.title: HTML Advanced Capstone
practical_project.brief: Build HTML Advanced Capstone using the skills from this course. Include a short explanation of your decisions, test the result on mobile and desktop, and make a small accessibility review.

final_assessment.title: HTML — Advanced final assessment
final_assessment.instructions: Complete the practical task, then answer the knowledge checks and explain two implementation decisions.
final_assessment.passing_guidance: Demonstrate the required structure, test the result, and explain why the chosen approach is appropriate.

teacher_materials.notes: Encourage learners to build from semantic structure, test incrementally, and explain their choices rather than copying patterns without understanding them.
teacher_materials.safety: Use only learner-owned or authorised files and environments.

provenance.content_note: Standalone HTML/CSS curriculum added to complement the existing Web Development pathway.
